name: Night Blue
lede: Night Blue is a dark, muted violet-blue standardized as RAL 5022 in Germany's 1927 color system, and its nearest named neighbor in our graph is a color we have already written about, [[adelaide]].

sections.title: A paint standard, and a crowd-sourced cousin
sections.body:
The German RAL system fixes Night Blue as RAL 5022, dated 1927 in our records; the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 place the same region in block 174 [1]. The crowd-labeled xkcd color survey, run in 2010, uses the same name for a noticeably darker, more saturated point, hex #040348, a reminder that "Night Blue" is not one fixed color across sources [1].

Our graph flags this name as contested, likely for the same reason: more than one modern source claims it for a different point [1]. Its nearest distinct named neighbor is [[adelaide]], 3.8 units off and "almost the same," with [[china-blue]] and [[cobalt-blue]] close by [3]. Our graph's own cross-reference for this region also lands near [[prussian-blue]], a darker, more storied blue with its own article here [3]. No book held in color-kb discusses "Night Blue" by this exact name [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Night Blue is rare in our archive: 17 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.07 percent, as photographed, and concentrated in the twentieth century, 5 times the base rate [2]. Russian works carry it at 8.5 times the archive's overall rate, the highest lift of any country we track for this color [2]. Counts are computed matches on varnished, photographed paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
